title: Establish adaptive pager cooldown and proactive capacity signals
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: During the 2026-02-21 capacity regression incident we observed a multi-region spike in token latency that generated cascading burn-rate pagers and repeated paging for the same underlying capacity event. This ticket defines the implementation and rollout plan for an adaptive pager cooldown that leverages fused signals (burn-rate, autoscaler activity, capacity headroom) and a lightweight root-cause aggregation signature to suppress repeat pages for the same incident while preserving visibility for genuine new regressions.

Goals: 1) Reduce duplicate/looping pagers from a single capacity regression by at least 80% in the first week post-rollout. 2) Avoid masking real customer-impacting regressions — detection latency should not increase by more than 30s for tier-0 incidents. 3) Introduce a deterministic signature for capacity events so related alerts are grouped in the console and can be auto-linked to postmortem artifacts.

Design notes: - Adaptive cooldown: cooldown window computed from recent burn-rate slope, request fanout, and autoscaler actions. Short spikes => short cooldown; sustained burns => longer, but capped at 30 minutes. - Signal fusion: combine Prometheus burn-rate metric, autoscaler webhook events, and node-level capacity headroom metrics (GPU memory, queue latency) into a single likelihood score. - Root-cause aggregation: lightweight hash of (model-version fingerprint + region + top-5 error traces + autoscaler-event-id) used to group related alerts and avoid re-paging. - Staged escalation: update Alertmanager route to implement staged paging (notify on-call layer 1 after initial threshold; escalate only if signature changes or cooldown expires). - Fall-through: if platform detects signed severity (P0 path) or manual override, normal paging proceeds.

Trade-offs considered: - Risk of increased time-to-detect for rare fast-failure regressions vs benefit of dramatically reduced pager noise. Mitigation: tiered cooldowns with strict 0s cooldown for tier-0 SLOs and conservative caps for higher tiers. - Complexity: additional signals require more instrumentation and a small runtime burden on the telemetry pipeline. We limit scope to aggregated metrics and autoscaler webhook metadata to keep overhead low.

Artifacts: design doc and telemetry spec: https://confluence.redwood.company/display/INF/Adaptive+Pager+Cooldown+Design, proposed Alertmanager change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/2871, experimental dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/alerting/adaptive-cooldown-experiment, incident runbook updates: https://drive.redwood.company/drive/folders/1a2b3c-adaptive-cooldown-runbooks

Rollout plan: 1) Feature-flagged canary for 2 weeks in us-west only (low-risk customers) 2) Monitor burn-rate alerts triage dashboard and on-call feedback 3) Expand to multi-region with 48h observation windows 4) Full rollout and deprecation of legacy suppression rules.

Acceptance criteria: - Canary reduces repeated pages from the Feb-21 signature by >=80% within 72 hours. - No >10% increase in mean time-to-detect for tier-1 SLOs during canary. - Dashboard shows correct grouping and links to the alert signature for aggregated incidents.
postmortem_action_items: Instrument autoscaler webhook IDs in telemetry and persist last-2 events per region
Implement cooldown calculator service (feature-flagged) and expose config in Console
Add deterministic signature generation to alert pipeline and link to incident console
Modify Alertmanager routes for staged escalation and implement suppression predicates
Update incident runbooks with new grouping behavior and manual override instructions
Create monitoring alerts for potential over-suppression (sensitivity regression)

implementation_notes: Keep signature deterministic and idempotent to avoid re-grouping when non-actionable metadata changes.
Expose cooldown parameters as runtime config with per-customer overrides for dedicated/private deployments.
Fallback to legacy behavior if telemetry stream misses autoscaler metadata for >5 minutes.
Limit suppression to alerts with identical signature and matching model-version fingerprint to avoid cross-model masking.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-suppression hides new regressions -> Mitigation: strict tier-0 bypass and automatic re-alert if error-rate slope increases during suppression
Risk: Telemetry lag leads to incorrect cooldown decisions -> Mitigation: prefer event-driven autoscaler webhooks over slow aggregates
Risk: Increased operational complexity -> Mitigation: provide runbook snippets and Console toggle to disable adaptive cooldown per-team
